children: Medium-sour coastal grades weakened on Wednesday to COVID-19 levels, dealers said, as high freight rates, easing supply constraints in the Middle East and lower prices for Canadian crude cut into demand.
Mars dipped to a discount of $7.50 to US West Texas Intermediate crude, the lowest since June 2022, while Southern Green Canyon eased to a discount of $8, the lowest since April.

Wednesday also marked the second day of the volatile roll-trade period in which traders square positions, adjust slates and net out any exposure. Prices to roll positions from October to November traded at $5.60.

Soaring freight rates for tankers that move oil from US to Europe and Asia have curbed demand for the oil, while Saudi Arabia resumed operations on its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea on Tuesday, easing some supply tightness.
Prices for Western Canada Select crude oil to North American benchmark West Texas Intermediate futures
have also widened in recent days after Exxon Mobil's
264,000-barrel-per-day Joliet, Illinois refinery went offline. The plant was restarting key units this week.

The US Department of Energy is expected to offer more oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve that competes with the gulf coast medium sour grades.  The department has loaned out about 132 million barrels of oil as part of its promise to release 172 million barrels, with the additional barrels expected to be offered soon.
Light Louisiana Sweet for October delivery was unchanged at a midpoint of a $2.50 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $2.00 and $3.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
Mars Sour eased $3 to a midpoint of a $7.5 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $7.75 and $7.25 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures
WTI Midland eased 40 cents to a midpoint of a 20-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between  parity and 40-cent​ a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
West Texas Sour dipped 40 cents to a midpoint of a $2.3 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $2.50 and $2.10 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures
WTI at East Houston , also known as MEH, traded between a 70-cent and $1.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
